# Economics model — preparation tiers and servicer throughput

**Generated by** `tools/generate_model_docs.py` from `v4_1_validation` (model `Phase2-RPO-MC-v4.1`). Re-run after any new campaign or assumption change.

> **Read this first.** Every money, mass, price and probability input in section 1 is an **ASSUMPTION** made to give the proposal a calculable first-pass economics. None is a ClearSpace figure, a vendor quote or customer data. What is *calculated from the simulator* is: per-attempt outcome probabilities, delta-v, propellant, and the beacon mass. Results are expected values under these inputs, not forecasts. This implements Guide §16's design-for-value rule (discounted incremental benefit vs interface mass, integration and servicing price) for one GEO client; ECON-01 is **partly** addressed — real costs, downtime and risk remain open.

Retries are allowed only after a *complete* retreat. An incomplete retreat (estimate mismatch) or violation ends the mission and carries the assumed collision-cost risk. This uses the v4.1 retreat outcomes that the earlier retry plot had to mark `n/a`.

## 3. Servicing success within 3 attempts and expected value per client at 3°/s

Value of one successful rescue, net of the servicing price, discounted to launch: **€20.84 M**. Expected value = P(needs rescue) × (P(success) × value − collision risk cost) − add-on cost.

| Tier | P(success) | P(mission lost) | Expected attempts | Benefit €M | Add-on cost €M | Net €M |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| C0 unprepared | 64.0% | 29.6% | 1.56 | 1.29 | 0.00 | 1.29 |
| C1 fiducials | 97.9% | 2.1% | 1.06 | 2.04 | 0.04 | 1.99 |
| C2 beacon (rate) | 100.0% | 0.0% | 1.00 | 2.08 | 0.40 | 1.68 |
| C3 IOS mode | 100.0% | 0.0% | 1.00 | 2.08 | 1.15 | 0.94 |

**Reading:** with retries, fiducials already recover most of the value at 3°/s; the beacon's extra benefit is small there, and IOS mode costs more than it returns unless a rescue is likely or the client tumbles faster. At 5°/s only C3 can be serviced at all (it assumes the client can damp itself). The beacon is likely **undervalued** here: its non-RPO benefits (identity, interface location, health flags, knowing the client state before committing a servicer) and the fully degraded case are not in the simulator, so they carry no value in this table.

## 4. Break-even probability that a client ever needs rescue

Smallest P(needs rescue) at which the extra tier cost is repaid by its extra expected benefit (lower is easier to justify).

| Tumble | C1 vs C0 | C2 vs C1 | C3 vs C2 | C3 vs C0 |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2°/s | 4.91% | never | never | >100% (not repaid) |
| 3°/s | 0.60% | 75.20% | never | 14.50% |
| 5°/s | 9.38% | >100% (not repaid) | 3.55% | 5.34% |

## 6. Servicer throughput (finite resources, Guide §16)

Servicer 3500 kg wet, 1500 kg usable propellant, Isp 320 s, 60 m/s per GEO transfer, 45 days per visit, 12-year life. Propellant by Δv = Isp·g0·ln(m₀/m₁). Break-even price = (capex + operations) ÷ expected successful services. Only fuel and time limits are modelled; delivered refuel inventory, POD cargo and risk reserve are not.

| Tumble | Tier | Propellant per visit kg | Visits (fuel/time limit) | Expected successful services | Break-even price per success €M |
|--:|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 3°/s | C0 unprepared | 68.8 | 21 (fuel) | 13.4 | 32.01 |
| 3°/s | C1 fiducials | 68.1 | 22 (fuel) | 21.5 | 19.97 |
| 3°/s | C2 beacon (rate) | 67.9 | 22 (fuel) | 22.0 | 19.55 |
| 3°/s | C3 IOS mode | 67.4 | 22 (fuel) | 22.0 | 19.55 |
| 5°/s | C0 unprepared | 69.7 | 21 (fuel) | 0.0 | n/a (no success) |
| 5°/s | C1 fiducials | 70.3 | 21 (fuel) | 0.0 | n/a (no success) |
| 5°/s | C2 beacon (rate) | 70.4 | 21 (fuel) | 0.0 | n/a (no success) |
| 5°/s | C3 IOS mode | 67.4 | 22 (fuel) | 22.0 | 19.55 |

| Tier | Provisions | Unit €M | Mass kg | Launch €M | NRE share €M | Total €M |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 EOL-ready | capture fixture + fiducials | 0.17 | 3.5 | 0.10 | 0.09 | 0.36 |
| 2 Service-ready | + IOS mode + beacon | 0.82 | 5.3 | 0.16 | 0.48 | 1.46 |
| 3 Life-extension-ready | + refuelling port | 1.42 | 9.3 | 0.28 | 0.48 | 2.18 |
| 4 Augmentation-ready | + OSAN (power/data/POD) | 4.42 | 34.3 | 1.03 | 1.24 | 6.68 |

Tiers 3–4 have **no benefit model here** (refuel/POD value needs a fuel-price, lifetime-extension and POD-capability model); their cost is shown for the roadmap trade only.

## 8. What this does and does not establish

* Establishes a transparent calculation chain from simulator outcomes to € per client, and which inputs matter (P(needs rescue) and servicing price dominate).
* Does **not** establish real prices, demand, insurance effects, downtime cost, or that clients would pay for preparation. Replace section-1 values with ClearSpace/operator data before any external claim.
* Avoids double counting: benefit is the retained contribution of the extension net of the price paid; replacement-satellite avoidance is not added on top.
